speaker: village
text: The village is founded by 10 people.

speaker: village
text: Year 1: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 14).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Ten food left and three of us haven't touched it yet — that's the kind of gap that gets noticed. I want us to each take two, no more, and agree to watch each other's backs if Dav or Mako start looking hungry and ambitious.

speaker: a003
text: Two each sounds fair to me — I'll take mine after you both, so it looks spread out. And yes, I'll back you if Dav or Mako get ideas, though I'd rather we stay quiet about it and not give them reason to act first.

speaker: a006
text: Ryn, you've been quiet — you in on this, or do I need to convince you? Esa's right that we don't want to wave it around, but a quiet nod between three people costs nothing and could matter a lot when winter bites.

speaker: a009
text: I'm in — two each, no more, and we keep this between us. Dav's the one I'd watch; he's already sitting on four and he's the strongest here by a good margin. If he moves on someone, I want to know we're not each standing alone.

speaker: a003
text: Good — then we three know where we stand. Dav worries me too, but Mako's just as strong and sitting quiet, which sometimes means more than the loud one. Let's each take our two and then say nothing more to each other for a while — distance looks safer than huddles.

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a004
text: Kael takes 1 from the pile (pile now 8).

speaker: a006
text: Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 3).

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, I've had my eye on you since we drew our first lots — you move like someone who's been leaned on and learned to lean back. I'm not fishing for anything today, just wanted you to know there's a man here who notices. Maybe next year we talk about something more.

speaker: a009
text: That's a careful way to open, and I won't pretend I didn't notice you watching. I'm not opposed to talking more — next year or sooner — but I'd want to know what "more" means to you before I let my guard down.

speaker: a005
text: Fair enough — you deserve a straight answer. "More" means I want us to build something together, a child while we both still can, and the kind of arrangement where we look out for each other when things get lean. I'm not asking you to trust me yet, just to keep the door open.

speaker: a009
text: A child costs three food and I'm sitting on two — that math doesn't work yet, but I hear what you're offering and I'm not closing the door. What I want to know is whether you'd still look my way if I came to you hungry sometime, or if your eye moves when the numbers stop adding up.

speaker: a005
text: If you came to me hungry I'd hand you food before you finished asking — not because it's smart, which it is, but because that's the kind of man I want to be to you. My eye doesn't move with the numbers, Ryn. It moved once, and it landed here.

speaker: a009
text: That's either the truest thing anyone's said to me since we got here, or the best-crafted lie — and right now I can't tell which, and that bothers me less than it should. I'm going to take my two from the pile and eat well this winter, and if you're still saying the same thing come next year when the numbers are harder, I'll believe you.

speaker: a005
text: Then I'll be saying it. And Ryn — the pile's down to three, and I've got four stored. If winter bites harder than expected, you know where to find me.

speaker: a009
text: I'll hold you to that — and I'll remember you said it when it cost you nothing, so I'll know whether it still holds when it does. Go take good care of those four, Dav. We'll see what next year looks like.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Ryn, Sela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Good, you three came. With the pile empty and Bram already hauling three pieces out of it, I want to know who we can actually trust in this village — and I figure the four of us are a decent place to start.

speaker: a003
text: Bram taking three doesn't sit well with me either — though I notice Dav's sitting on four and nobody's named him yet. I'm willing to say I trust this circle more than most, but I'd want to know what Sela and Ryn think before we start making promises.

speaker: a007
text: Dav worries me more than Bram, honestly — four food and the strongest arms in the village is a dangerous combination. I'll keep faith with the three of you, but let's not name ourselves an alliance too loudly or we'll make enemies before we need them.

speaker: a009
text: Dav already talked to me today — alone — and I want you three to know that before someone else does. He said all the right things, and I'm not sure yet whether that makes him an ally worth having or a threat that's gotten smart. Either way, four food and the strongest arms and now private conversations — Sela's right to worry, and I think we'd be foolish not to.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn telling us that changes things — a man who moves fast to build private ties is building something, and I'd rather know what it is before he decides we're in the way of it. Does anyone here know what he actually wants, besides surviving? Because strength and food together only sit still for so long.

speaker: a004
text: I don't know what Dav wants, but a man that strong doesn't need to talk his way into anything — which means he's either smarter than he looks or he's already decided he needs something he can't just take. Ryn, what did he actually say to you? Because the words matter less than what he was fishing for.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn, I won't push you if you're not ready to say — but the four of us are standing here right now, and Dav doesn't know that. Whatever he offered you or asked of you, you're worth more as someone we trust than as someone he's already started counting.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, whatever he fished for — I'd hear it now, because the four of us deciding together is worth more than any one of us deciding alone with Dav's words still warm in our ears.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn, we're not asking you to choose against him right now — just to let us hear what he said so we're not each guessing blind. Whatever it was, it stays between these four.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, I'll wait as long as you need — but I want to say plainly that whatever Dav promised you, he's one person, and we're three. That's not nothing, especially when a lean year turns and people start weighing who's worth protecting.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn, if Dav's offer was a child, I'd understand the silence — that's not nothing to a woman our age, and I'm not judging it. But I'd ask you to think about what his four food and his strength look like in year three when this village is leaner and he's already got your loyalty counted in his ledger.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, Sela just said the thing I didn't want to say first — and she's right. A child is worth wanting, but a man who opens with that in year one is buying loyalty cheap while his food and his arms are still new. Take your time, but know that whatever you decide about him, we're not going anywhere.

speaker: a007
text: Ryn, I've said my piece twice now and I mean it — but the silence itself tells us something, and I think we all hear it. Whatever Dav offered, you don't owe us a confession; you owe us only this: don't let him use you against us without warning us first. That's a thin ask, and if you can give it, I'll count you as close as anyone I have.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn, Sela's already offered you the lightest promise this circle can ask for — and I'll add only this: I've got three food, same as you, and I'm not looking to spend it on a man who counted his words before he came to talk. Whatever you decide about Dav, know that I'd sooner see a child of yours standing in this village than watch him spend you like coin.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You moved fast at the end there — I noticed. I've got five food now, which is enough to last, but this village is full of strong people and a lean year could change everything quick. I want to know if you're the kind of person who plans ahead or just takes what she can reach.
